title: How many squares remain at Step three and Step four?
description: The video starts from the sixty four squares of Step two and uses the rule that every remaining square gives eight at the next step. It multiplies by eight twice to reach Step three and Step four. Keeko's doubt is that each step only adds eight squares.
teaching_notes: One idea: the squares of one step are multiplied by eight to get the next step. Watch for students who add eight to the count instead of multiplying.

source: Find the number of remaining squares at Step 3 and at Step 4
video_script.why: The child has the squares of Step two and now uses the book's rule to go further.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the squares of one step by eight to get the next step.
video_script.anchor: the {{NAME_2}} Carpet of the book, shown as a table of steps and remaining squares
video_script.wrong_answer: Step three has seventy two squares
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds eight to the sixty four squares of Step two and says Step three has seventy two squares. Every remaining square gives eight squares, so the count is multiplied by eight.
video_script.payoff_line: Step three has five hundred and twelve squares and Step four has four thousand and ninety six

final_answer.value: 512 squares at Step 3 and 4096 at Step 4
final_answer.spoken: five hundred and twelve squares at Step three and four thousand and ninety six at Step four

names.{{NAME_2}}: Polish mathematician who discovered the carpet and the triangle

hold_back: Answer: 512 squares at Step 3 and 4096 squares at Step 4
maths_rules: rule from the book: R(n+1) = 8 x R(n)
video_script.design: A table of steps and remaining squares grows one row at a time, with an arrow marked times eight between rows.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the {{NAME_2}} Carpet.
<bookmark mark='known'/>At Step two, the carpet has sixty four squares that remain.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many squares remain at Step three, and how many at Step four?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board with the two empty rows underlined

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: one remaining square is cut into a 3 by 3 grid; its central square is removed and 8 squares stay

marks.one: one remaining square is cut into three rows of three
marks.eight: the central square fades and the eight left glow
marks.rule: the words each square gives 8 squares are written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Take any one square that remains at some step.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>At the next step, it is cut into nine and loses its central square, so eight squares stay.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>Every remaining square gives eight squares at the next step.

beats.on_screen: Given: Step 2 has 64 remaining squares. Each remaining square gives 8 squares at the next step.

marks.given: the sixty four squares and the rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Step two has sixty four remaining squares, and each one gives eight squares at the next step.

beats.on_screen: To find: remaining squares at Step 3 and at Step 4

marks.find: the words Step 3 and Step 4 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remaining squares at Step three and at Step four.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: squares of Step 2 x 8 = 64 x 8 = 512

marks.rule: the line squares of Step 2 times 8 is written
marks.calc: 64 x 8 = 512 is written and the row for Step 3 is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, multiply the squares of Step two by eight, because each square gives eight.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Sixty four times eight is five hundred and twelve.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: squares of Step 3 x 8 = 512 x 8 = 4096

marks.rule: the line squares of Step 3 times 8 is written
marks.calc: 512 x 8 = 4096 is written and the row for Step 4 is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, multiply the squares of Step three by eight in the same way.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Five hundred and twelve times eight is four thousand and ninety six.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 512 squares at Step 3 and 4096 squares at Step 4
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Step three has five hundred and twelve squares and Step four has four thousand and ninety six.
<bookmark mark='row'/>Each step has eight times the squares of the step before.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the table
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 64 + 8 = 72, struck through; the jump from 8 to 64 in the table flashes

marks.look: the jump from 8 to 64 in the table flashes
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the arrows marked times 8 return

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks Step three has seventy two squares, after adding eight to sixty four.
<bookmark mark='look'/>Look at the table. Step one has eight squares, and Step two has sixty four, not sixteen.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Every square breaks into eight, so the count is multiplied by eight.
